topic: Evernorth's 2026-10-22 outbound XRP transfers: destination-wallet activation and multisig cross-check

evidence_policy.ledger_attribution: XRP Insights public rippled JSON-RPC snapshot

source_snapshot.limitation: XRP Insights is a secondary attribution layer. Its source/destination wallet labels are publisher classifications; transaction hashes and balances are public ledger observations, but the full history was not independently replayed in this run.

destinations.activation_wallet: unknown; Bithomp account page retrieval failed

destination_reconciliation.method: Sum all 19 source transactions by destination. For nine destinations, Bithomp public account pages show activation by the same BitGo-labelled wallet rD4G6gtD2KwHqsRf7pcyA8r1neUzXT61ix and multisig account control. The remaining destination rPjK has a matching ~42.26382M balance in Bithomp's rich list, but its account page could not be retrieved; no BitGo activation claim is made for it.

custody_interpretation.finding: At least 328.083M XRP, or 88.59% of the 370.347M gross outbound transfers reported by XRP Insights, was sent to nine destination accounts that Bithomp says were activated by a BitGo-labelled wallet and have multisig control. Six large destinations were activated within a 4m20s window on October 20; three smaller destinations were activated on October 12. This pattern strongly supports BitGo-created custody/multisig redistribution rather than ordinary exchange deposits or demonstrated sale.
custody_interpretation.primary_context: Evernorth's SEC prospectus says all XRP was initially held in BitGo custody accounts, 100% offline/cold as of prospectus date, and segregated for Evernorth's benefit.
not_established: BitGo's legal beneficial ownership or ongoing signer control of each destination
That every destination is still within BitGo custody today
The identity/control of the remaining rPjK destination
Whether any funds were subsequently deployed, pledged or lent under an expressly directed yield strategy
Whether any destination later transferred XRP to an exchange or counterparty

accounting_warning.explanation: The gross outbound amount is the sum of 19 payments, not a unique net-disposition figure. Some destinations are BitGo-activated multisig wallets, so subsequent custody transfers can be intermediate hops. The 200,138 XRP excess remains unresolved and must not be forced into the 200,000 delayed-funding tranche.
accounting_warning.required_reconciliation: Trace all destination histories through a later validated ledger; deduplicate intermediate transfers, classify returned flows, and reconcile each wallet's balance changes to the SEC closing holdings.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The majority of Evernorth's reported external outflows were internal BitGo custody/multisig redistribution.
support: Nine destination accounts receiving 328.083M XRP were activated by the same BitGo-labelled wallet
Those nine accounts show multisig control and no usernames
SEC prospectus identifies BitGo as custodian and states 100% cold storage
Six large destinations were activated within a 4m20s window on Oct20
counterevidence: Bithomp activation by BitGo does not independently prove legal custody or current signer control
Destination transaction histories were not fully replayed
11.41% of gross outflow goes to an address whose activation could not be verified
hypotheses.test: Obtain destination account transaction histories and signer lists at pinned ledgers; compare to BitGo custody disclosure and subsequent Evernorth filings.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some XRP may have moved to an execution or yield strategy partner as part of Q4 deployment.
support: Evernorth announced Q4 deployment with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo
Large outbound transfers occurred in October
counterevidence: At least 88.59% of gross outflows target BitGo-activated multisig accounts
No destination is attributed to Coinbase, Kraken or Ripple in the current evidence
hypotheses.test: Require partner-specific public disclosure or a verified destination/transaction attribution before assigning an execution edge.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The outflows represent XRP sales or exchange deposits.
support: Transfers left the original 13-wallet attributed set
counterevidence: Nine destinations are BitGo-activated multisig accounts
No exchange deposit address has been identified
SEC custody disclosure and multisig pattern support custody movement
hypotheses.test: Do not accept without exchange/dealer attribution, subsequent fiat/stablecoin consideration or issuer disclosure.

feature_store_rules: Track source wallet, destination wallet, transaction hash, amount, ledger index, timestamp, BitGo activation wallet, activation timestamp and multisig status separately.
A destination outside the issuer-attributed wallet set is not automatically an external custodian, exchange, counterparty or sale.
Classify BitGo-activated multisig destinations as strong custody inference, not issuer-confirmed custody.
Keep gross transfer volume separate from unique net outflow and ending balance.
Deduplicate intermediate hops before computing treasury disposition or sale metrics.
Preserve the 11.41% unresolved destination as unknown until direct public-ledger replay or issuer evidence resolves it.
Do not infer deployment to Coinbase/Kraken/Ripple from the mere fact of a transfer.

forecast.reason: The evidence changes the custody interpretation but does not establish a directional price edge.

next_actions: Replay all nine BitGo-activated destinations and the unresolved rPjK address at the latest validated ledger.
Verify signer lists and subsequent outgoing transactions for each destination.
Trace whether any destination later sends XRP to Coinbase, Kraken, Ripple, exchanges, AMMs, vaults or loan brokers.
Reconcile the 200,138 XRP gross-flow excess and distinguish intermediate custody hops from unique final disposition.
Update Evernorth custody graph only to STRONG_INFERENCE until issuer confirmation is available.
safety: Public SEC filings, public XRPL transaction data and public account explorer metadata only. No private custody access, credential use, exchange access, trading or real-money activity.
